conventions.convention: At a rational point the cotangent space is m/m² over the residue field, and the intrinsic tangent space is its dual; tangent vectors correspond to dual-number points.
The Jacobian uses equation rows and coordinate columns, and uses the actual scheme ideal without replacing it by its radical.
Regularity is regular-local-ring regularity; smoothness over a field is geometric regularity. The regular-smooth equivalence here is qualified by a perfect base field.
The tangent cone is defined by the full associated graded ideal, and hypersurface multiplicity is the degree of the lowest nonzero homogeneous term.
The characteristic-zero generic-smoothness conclusion over a dense target open uses the stated smooth-source hypothesis.
Bertini smoothness is asserted away from the base locus, under the theorem's stated field and linear-system hypotheses.
The dualizing line bundle is ω_X = det Ω¹_{X/k}; the trace is normalized through the projective embedding and its residue/Koszul data.
The embedding Gysin/Koszul orientation uses σ_c = (−1)^{c(c+1)/2}.
The Borel-character line bundle is L_λ = G×^B C_{−λ}, so its fibre at eB has character −λ.
The canonical bundle of G/B has weight −2ρ; for G/B → G/P_α the relative canonical bundle has weight −α and degree −2 on each P¹ fibre.
The degree of L_λ on the minimal-parabolic P¹ fibre is +⟨λ,α∨⟩.
The Fourier transform uses the negative 2π sign; it is unitary on L², with translation symbol e^(−2πia·ξ) and derivative symbol 2πiξ.

The Lᵖ multiplier definition is for finite p; the Mihlin symbol requires q = floor(n/2)+1 derivatives off the origin, leaves its value at zero free, and does not itself assert an Lᵖ boundedness theorem.
H^s uses the Japanese-bracket weight ⟨ξ⟩^s, not the Laplacian weight (1+4π²|ξ|²)^(s/2); the Sobolev pairing is first-variable-linear.
The weak-derivative test pairing is bilinear without conjugation; W^{0,p}=L^p and both p=1 and p=∞ are included.

load_bearing.statement: At a rational point of an affine scheme cut out by an ideal I, the intrinsic tangent space is the kernel of the evaluated Jacobian map for I; equivalently its vectors annihilate the differentials at that point of all equations in I.
Over a perfect field, a finite-type scheme is smooth over the field if and only if its local rings are regular.
For a dominant morphism of finite-type varieties over a characteristic-zero field with smooth source, there is a dense open of the target over which the morphism is smooth.
Under the theorem's stated field, smoothness, and linear-system hypotheses, a general member is smooth at every point outside the base locus.

For a smooth projective variety X of dimension n with normalized trace t_X:H^n(X,ω_X)→k and a locally free sheaf E, the cup-product-and-trace pairing H^q(X,E) × H^{n−q}(X,E∨⊗ω_X)→k is perfect for every q.
For a Zariski locally trivial P¹-bundle π and a line bundle L of fibre degree n≥−1, H^i(E,L) is naturally isomorphic to H^{i+1}(E,L⊗K_π^(n+1)); when n=−1 both sides vanish.
For integer k≥0 on R^n, W^{k,2} and H^k agree as spaces with equivalent norms, under the stated weak-derivative and Fourier conventions.
For real s, H^s(R^n) consists exactly of tempered distributions u for which ⟨ξ⟩^s Fu is an L² regular distribution; its H^s norm equals the L² norm of that weighted Fourier transform.

concerns.concern: Step 1.6 calls C_r a closed subvariety of X and uses its finite irreducible-component decomposition before steps 2.1 and 3.1 establish global closedness; up to then the proof has shown only local closedness. A locally closed-subvariety argument may suffice for Noetherianity and finite components, but the proof should state that justification or establish closedness before relying on it.
